title: Boyle's law: pressure and volume (constant temperature)
summary: Squeeze a gas slowly: pressure rises as volume falls, and P × V stays the same.
alt: A cylinder with a piston and a P–V graph showing the curve P = k/V with a live dot and a rectangle whose area is P times V.

gas.label: Gas molecules
gas.text: The molecules of the gas (colour = speed: blue slow, red fast).

me.label: Live reading
me.text: What the simulated gas shows right now.

work.label: P × V area
work.text: The area of this rectangle is P × V and does not change.

steps.title: Gas trapped in a cylinder
steps.text: A fixed amount of gas is trapped in a cylinder. We keep the **temperature constant**, so the molecules keep the same average speed. Only the volume changes. The pressure is {{Pm|2}} × P₀.

steps.title: Push the piston in
steps.text: Push the piston in slowly. The gas has less room, so molecules hit the piston **more often**. The pressure **rises**: look at the red dot climbing the curve.

steps.title: Half the volume, double the pressure
steps.text: At V = {{L/8|2}} V₀ the pressure is {{Pm|2}} P₀. Halve the volume and the pressure **doubles**.

steps.title: Pull the piston out
steps.text: Now let the gas expand. More room means fewer hits, so the pressure **drops** along the same curve.

steps.title: P × V never changes
steps.text: The shaded rectangle changes shape, but its **area (P × V) stays the same**. The curve is a hyperbola: \( PV = \text{constant} \).

steps.title: Hotter gas, higher curve
steps.text: Raising the temperature does not break the law: it moves the whole curve **up**. Each temperature has its own curve, called an **isotherm**. Explore with the sliders.

formulas.title: Boyle's law
formulas.text: At constant temperature and amount of gas, P × V stays the same.

formulas.title: Same thing, as a graph
formulas.text: P against V is a curve (hyperbola); P against 1/V is a straight line through the origin.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A gas at **2 atm** is squeezed from **6 L** to **3 L** at constant temperature. What is the new pressure in atm?

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: The gas is at **1 P₀** when V = V₀. What pressure (in P₀) will it show when the volume is made **one quarter** of V₀?
challenges.hint: Quarter the volume = four times the pressure.
challenges.explain: P × V is constant, so \( P = 4 \) P₀.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: Which statement is true for a gas at **constant temperature**?

options.label: P and V are directly proportional
P and V are inversely proportional
P and V are always equal
P does not depend on V

challenges.hint: When one goes up the other goes down.
challenges.explain: Boyle's law: P × V = constant, so P ∝ 1/V.

takeaways: **Boyle's law:** at constant temperature, \( PV = \text{constant} \) for a fixed amount of gas.
Smaller volume means more frequent hits, so **higher pressure**.
The P–V graph of constant temperature is a **hyperbola**, called an isotherm.

notes.title: Connects to
notes.text: Boyle's curve is the **isothermal process** (T constant, ΔU = 0). The **area under** a P–V curve is the work done: see *Work as area under P–V*. Compare with Charles and Gay-Lussac, where temperature changes.
